_comment: ngsolve dg_methods#6 (advection makes the DG matrix unsymmetric; CG is the wrong solver). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh 0.2, L2 order 1, SIP diffusion alone vs the same form plus b=(20,0) upwind advection, CG and GMRes both from ngsolve.krylovspace with the same CreateSmoother preconditioner and maxiter 500, reference from the umfpack direct solve. Pure diffusion is symmetric to 4.7e-17 and CG converges in 105 iterations to 2.6e-12. With advection the relative asymmetry is 9.8e-2. CORRECTION: the claim offers two alternative signals and only one occurs. CGSolver raises NOTHING -- no exception, no 'not positive definite' message anywhere in the run. It returns normally after consuming all 500 iterations with a relative error of 208 against the direct solve, i.e. a field two orders of magnitude larger than the answer. An agent guarding on an exception, the first branch the claim names, sees a clean solve and ships the wrong field. GMRes on the same matrix and preconditioner converges in 98 iterations to 2.0e-11. Mutation: dropping the advection terms makes CG converge and the fixture fails on advection_breaks_symmetry and cg_fails_silently_not_loudly. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 skips the three advection integrals in build() (the 'if with_advection' block), so the with_advection system is the pure SIP diffusion operator again. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 9 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 drops the relative asymmetry to 4.7e-17 and CG converges in 105 iterations, removing 'advection_breaks_symmetry=True', 'cg_exhausted_its_iteration_cap=True', 'cg_relative_error_exceeds_the_solution=True' and 'cg_fails_silently_not_loudly=True' so the fixture goes red. CAVEAT: 'cg_emitted_positive_definite_message' is evaluated against the caught exception text only, which is empty by construction when nothing is raised; no NGSolve stdout/stderr is scanned, so it does not establish the '_comment' claim that no such message appears anywhere in the run. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py FIXED 2026-08-08 (assertion changed): cg_emitted_positive_definite_message was any(p in (exc_cg_a or '').lower() for p in NOT_PD_PHRASES) -- computed from the caught exception's text ONLY. That text is '' exactly when the co-asserted cg_raised_on_unsymmetric_matrix=False holds, so the two expectations were one measurement printed twice and neither ever looked at what CGSolver WROTE. The claim being corrected says CG 'raises a matrix not positive definite error', and a library can emit that message without raising, so the message channel has to be read. The solve now runs inside an fd-level capture (os.dup2 on fd 1 and 2, so C++ printing is caught too) and the flag is the union over {exception text, captured stdout+stderr}. THREE CONTROLS, all executed 2026-08-08 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: (1) CAPTURE PROOF -- re-run with printrates=True, with_advection_cg_printed_bytes=28181 and cg_printed_during_solve shows NGSolve's own 'CG iteration n, residual = ...' lines, so the capture demonstrably sees this library's output and the 0 bytes measured in the real run is a measurement rather than a blind spot; (2) INJECTION -- emit 'CGSolver: matrix not positive definite' on fd 2 during the solve WITHOUT raising: cg_raised_on_unsymmetric_matrix stays False while cg_positive_definite_message_channels=['stdout_stderr'] and the flag flips to True, FAIL raised, rc=2, which is the case the old code could not see at all; (3) TAUTOLOGY CONTROL -- the same injected run with the line replaced by a literal print('cg_emitted_positive_definite_message=False'): the expectation survives. Unmutated the flag is False with cg_printed_during_solve='' and 0 bytes: NGSolve's CGSolver really does say nothing, which is the finding this fixture exists for.
